title: Construction Services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage St. Elizabeths West Campus
description: Amendment 0003 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0002 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0001 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is seeking a qualified contractor for construction services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage at the St. Elizabeths West Campus in Southeast Washington, DC. GSA anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price construction contract for the new construction of the Gate 7 Parking Garage and associated site, utility, security, stormwater, landscape, and infrastructure improvements. The project will support the operational needs of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at the St. Elizabeths West Campus. This acquisition is for construction services only. The project design is being completed separately by GSA�s Architect of Record, ZGF. The construction solicitation is based on Issued for Construction drawings, specifications, and related contract documents. The work to be performed under the terms of this contract includes, but is not limited to, furnishing all management, supervision, subcontractors, labor, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, coordination, quality control, testing, inspections, commissioning support, and closeout documentation necessary to construct the Gate 7 Parking Garage in accordance with the contract documents. The project includes construction of a new multi-level parking garage with associated surface parking, access and screening infrastructure, and related campus improvements. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Site development, clearing, grading, excavation, and civil infrastructure improvements Utility relocations, extensions, tie-ins, and connections Substructure construction, including foundations, slab-on-grade, excavation support, waterproofing, and retaining walls Parking garage structure, including structural framing, parking decks, ramps, stairs, elevators, roof assemblies, and related structural components Mechanically ventilated parking garage systems, including ventilation equipment, shafts, ductwork, louvers or openings, controls, electrical power, life-safety interfaces, testing, balancing, and commissioning support Exterior fa�ade and building envelope construction, including a classical architectural brick fa�ade with openings Exterior doors, windows, louvers, waterproofing, sealants, flashings, and related envelope components Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, fire alarm, emergency communications, lighting, controls, IT, telecommunications, electronic security, access control, CCTV, parking guidance, and related systems Physical security elements, including vehicle barriers, bollards, gates, credentialing areas, and screening-related infrastructure Roadway, shuttle, pedestrian circulation, hardscape, landscape, site lighting, signage, and related site improvements Stormwater management facilities, erosion and sediment control, and environmental protection measures Testing, inspections, commissioning support, training, warranties, as-built documentation, BIM/COBie deliverables where applicable, and project closeout The Gate 7 Parking Garage will be constructed within the active St. Elizabeths West Campus, a high-security federal campus and National Historic Landmark. The contractor will be required to coordinate construction activities with ongoing campus operations, security requirements, occupied facilities, existing utilities, shuttle operations, adjacent work, traffic and access impacts, and protection of historic and environmental resources. The contractor may also be required to coordinate with District of Columbia agencies or authorities, as applicable, for traffic control, haul routes, public space, utility, roadway, permit, or other construction-related requirements. All work shall conform to applicable GSA requirements, the 2026 PBS Core Building Standards, contract drawings and specifications, campus security requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project-specific requirements. The estimated cost range for construction is between $120,000,000.00 and $160,000,000.00. The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Construction Concept. AMENDMENTS TO SOLICITATION: It is the offeror's responsibility to monitor SAM.gov for the release of any amendments. BONDING: A bid bond is required in Phase 2 as well as payment and performance bonds after award. SECURITY: Before employees are allowed to work under the anticipated contract, all personnel are required to pass a security check. Specific security requirements will be contained in the solicitation. FUNDS AVAILABILITY: Funds are not presently available for this contract. The Government�s obligation under this contract is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. No legal liability on the part of the Government arises until award of the contract. ELIGIBLE OFFERORS: All responsible business firms may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. All prospective offerors are also required to use the System for Award Management at SAM.gov for registering their firm and completing representations and certifications. Any questions regarding this notification shall be directed to Jennifer Silkensen, Contracting Officer, via email at jennifer.silkensen@gsa.gov. Potential offerors are responsible for monitoring and downloading the solicitation and any potential amendments, if any, to the solicitation.

description: This is a Small Business Sources Sought (SBSS) Notice for Research and Development (R&D). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified small businesses under the size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541715 � Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), and the small business size standard for such requirements is 1,000 employees or less, including applicable affiliates. This SBSS notice is for market research and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Government. The purpose of this synopsis is to identify small business organizations with requisite qualifications to provide the services stated herein. Based on capability statements received in response to this Sources Sought Announcement, this acquisition may be solicited as a small business set-aside. All small business organizations (SB, SDB, WOSB, HUBZone, VOSB, and SDVOSB) are encouraged to respond to this notice. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should not submit a response to this notice.

title: FAA Contract Tower (FCT) Aviation Liability Insurance- Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Federal Aviation Administration is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to invite industry input, feedback, and recommendations on the attached Draft Statement of Work (SOW) for brokerage services to acquire aviation liability insurance at current and future Federal Aviation Administration Contract Towers (FCTs), to include the future use of Digital Tower Systems. Industry is also encouraged to address the attached questions regarding the integration of Digital Tower Systems into the Aviation Liability Insurance program. This notice is published solely for planning and scope-refinement purposes. It does not constitute a Screening Information Request (SIR) or Request for Proposals of any kind. The primary goal of this release is to seek feedback from industry on the clarity, feasibility, and structure of the proposed requirements prior to issuing a final solicitation. The agency is not requesting general company capabilities, marketing materials, unsolicited proposals, or corporate overviews at this time. Feedback should focus specifically on the draft SOW requirements. Participation in this RFI is entirely voluntary. All information provided will be at no cost to the Government, and no reimbursement will be made for any materials or effort submitted. Responses should be submitted to the Contract Specialist, Jasmine.Royal@faa.gov no later than 4:00 PM ET, November 23, 2026. Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by email to Jasmine Royal at jasmine.royal@faa.gov and Chontice Boykin at chontice.boykin@faa.gov.

The required scope includes the design, fabrication, and delivery of custom protective inserts. (ix) Provisions and Clauses: The standard commercial provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition, include, but not limited to, the equivalents of FAR 52.212-1 (Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services), FAR 52.212-4 (Contract Terms and Conditions), and FAR 52.212-5 (Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders). Specific clauses will be detailed in the direct RFP sent to Transtar Aircraft Interiors LLC. title: Finland – Miscellaneous repair and maintenance services – Pesulakoneiden toimitukset ja asennukset sekä huoltotoiminnot / VAV
description: Tilaajan tavoitteena on hankkia joustava yhteistyökumppani Vantaalla sijaitsevien VAV-konsernin omistamien kiinteistöjen pesuloiden ja kuivaushuoneiden uusien koneiden toimituksiin, asennuksiin sekä niiden huoltotoimintoihin. Tarkemmin tiloihin ja laitekantaan voi tutustua oheisesta kohdeluettelosta. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden koneuusintoihin liittyviä toimeksiantoja esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 60 kpl / vuosi. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden konehuoltoihin liittyviä vikatarkastus-/korjauksia esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 360 kpl / vuosi, jonka lisäksi Tilaajalla on ennakoivaa vuosihuoltotoimintaa. Sopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta. Tilaaja ei sitoudu hankintailmoituksessa esitettyihin arvioihin hankintamääristä. Tilaaja pitää erityisen tärkeänä, että pesula- ja kuivaushuoneissa käytettävät koneet huolletaan systemaattisesti ("vuosihuollot"). Lisäksi arjessa esiintyvät muunlaiset vikakorjaukset tehdään ripeästi ja että koneet uusitaan elinkaariajattelu huomioiden kustannustehokkaasti. Uusien pesulakoneiden toimituksissa ja asennuksissa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden laitekannan uusiminen Tilaajan kanssa erikseen sopien Pesulakoneiden huoltotoiminnassa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Laitteiden ennakoiva vuosihuoltotoiminta • Kuivausrummun huoltotoimet vikaantumisissa • Pesukoneen poisto-/tuloputken huollot, virran antoon liittyvien vikojen selvittely ja ohjauspaneelien huolto-/ korjaustoimet • Mankelin erilaiset huolto-/korjaustoimet • Kuivaushuoneen puhaltimien virhetilanteiden hoitaminen Työtilauksiin voi sisältyä myös tarvikehankintoja ja muita työn suorittamiseen liittyviä palveluhankintoja. Tavoitteiden saavuttamisen edellytykset on kerrottu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön ESPD-lomakkeella, hankinnan kohteen kriteerit -osiossa sekä hankintailmoituksen liitteissä. Hankintapäätöksen tekoperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus pisteytyksen mukaisesti, jossa maksimipisteet ovat 1000 pistettä. Tarjoajan on annettava tarjous kaikista tarjouslomakkeen töistä. Mikäli Tarjoaja ei ole tarjonnut kaikkia tarjouslomakkeeseen eriteltyjä töitä, tulkitaan tarjous puutteelliseksi. Puutteellinen tarjous hylätään. Tarjoajan kannalta huomioitavaa on myös se, että tarjottujen töiden ja hintojen tulee sisältää kaikki tässä tarjouspyynnössä, hankintasopimusluonnoksessa ja palvelukuvauksessa määritellyt kriteerit. Palvelu toteutetaan tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja laatuvaatimusten mukaisesti. Tarjoajan antama tarjous on sitova. Hankintasopimus syntyy vasta kirjallisen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisella, selonottoneuvottelujen jälkeen. EU-kynnysarvon ylittävässä hankinnassa sopimus voidaan tehdä aikaisintaan 14 vuorokauden kuluttua siitä, kun Tarjoaja on saanut tai hänen katsotaan saaneen päätöksen perusteluineen tiedoksi. Tarjoaja ei saa esittää esimerkiksi omissa tarjousasiakirjoissaan ehtoja, jotka vaikuttaisivat hankintasopimuksen sisältöön. Sopimuskauden tavoitealkamisajankohta on 1.4.2027 ja sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi.

description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. The Naval Air Systems Command, PMA-262 (Program Office for MQ-4C Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS)), is soliciting information from industry to determine potential contractors who have the skills, experience, qualifications, and knowledge to provide the comprehensive engineering, logistics, material, maintenance, program management, and operational support required to successfully provide the sustaining and reach back engineering support needed to sustain the United States Navy and Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) MQ-4C Triton UAS at both Contiguous United States (CONUS) and Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS) locations. This effort includes up to higher than Secret classification level of support. Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (NGSC) is the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the MQ-4C Triton UAS. As such they possess the requisite technical data and knowledge to meet the Navy�s requirements for sustaining engineering support of the MQ-4C UAS. The contractor shall be responsible for obtaining from NGSC all manufacturing drawing and proprietary specification data necessary to support the sustainment of the MQ-4C Triton UAS. DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify interested sources capable of meeting the requirements. This RFI is issued solely for market research, planning and information purposes and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contractual agreement, nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. There is no commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation, make an award, or be responsible for any monies expended by any interested parties in support of the effort mentioned above. Vendors can additionally provide a capabilities statement of no more than five (5) pages in length that demonstrates the respondent�s ability to meet the requirements as specified herein. The Government is interested in receiving vendors� commercial published price lists for items they believe meet the need in this RFI. All data received in response to this RFI, marked or designated as corporate or proprietary, will be fully protected from release outside the Government. Failure to respond to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future associated RFP that may be issued. The capability statement should include, at a minimum, the following: Company Name, Company Address, Company Business Size, CAGE code, and Point of Contact (POC) information to include POC�s name, phone number and email address. Relevant past performance / experience. A concise description of the company�s experience providing sustaining engineering, logistics, material, maintenance, program management, and/or operational/reach-back support for military UAS or similarly complex aviation platforms, at CONUS and OCONUS locations. Include at least two specific examples (contract number/customer, period of performance, approximate value, locations, classification level, and a one- or two-sentence description of the work). Experience with High Altitude Long Endurance (HALE) UAS, maritime ISR systems, or OEM-unique designs is of particular interest but is not a prerequisite. Technical data access. Evidence of current access to, or a realistic plan for obtaining, the manufacturing drawings, proprietary specifications, and other technical data necessary to sustain the MQ-4C Triton UAS. description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Philadelphia District, intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office within the USACE Philadelphia (NAP) District area of responsibility in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor is responsible for scheduling work in accordance with the requirements of task order issued and during regular business hours when scheduling on site work. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. The Fort Mifflin Project Office is responsible for the construction of the district�s disposal areas located along the Delaware River. Our mission supports the deepening and the maintenance dredging of the Delaware River and Wilmington Harbor. Heavy Equipment is utilized to construct dikes, ditching for drying and other dirt work. Our equipment is currently composed of D6 Dozers, Excavators (tracks and pontoons), dump trucks (articulated). Without equipment to provide the necessary dirt work in these disposals� areas, dredging assignments in the Delaware Harbor could not be accomplished. It is important that dredging and proper disposal activities of dredge materials is accomplished because it directly effects commerce and the safety of vessels transporting commodities and other resources to the ports. title: PACA Special Audits RFQ
description: General The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians, and families. Air Force Services Center supports bases, major commands (MAJCOMs), and the Air Staff by providing technical expertise, launching new initiatives, developing programs and operational procedures, and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures the successful operation of essential food services, fitness and sports centers, childcare and youth programs, lodging accommodations, and recreational opportunities for military members and their families worldwide. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field, and developing new programs supporting installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) centrally manages and administers the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program, which supports a worldwide mission providing independent oversight of internal controls, cash management, asset protection, and financial management across the enterprise. Background Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families, and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery, operational readiness, and the protection of government interests. Regular independent audits are required to evaluate the financial condition, control environments, and operational efficiencies of Nonappropriated Fund operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations Branch (AFSVC/VFSF) exercises central program oversight to ensure compliance with annual statutory audit requirements under Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 7600.06, Audit of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities and Related Activities, ensuring adequate audit coverage is provided across the enterprise for Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The term "Activities" refers to operational and revenue-generating entities within the Air Force structure. Audit engagements under this Special Audits contract specifically include financial statement audits and performance audits covering: � Accounting practices and transactional compliance; � Internal control environments and segregation of duties; � Cash management, vault operations, and electronic banking; � Fixed asset accountability, tracking, and depreciation; � Inventory valuation, spoilage controls, and physical counts; � Food and beverage operations and food service portfolios; � Centralized shared service center processing; � Venture gaming and electronic slot machine operations; � Supplemental mission dining operations; and � Agreed-upon procedures and special interest compliance reviews. Shared Service Center (SSC): Conduct performance audits of the Shared Service Center (SSC) at the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) located in San Antonio, TX. The primary objective of the performance audit is to address economy, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The scope includes core accounting transaction workflows, inter-entity cost allocation methodologies, compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operational metrics, and the adequacy of financial management technology system controls. Further details will be outlined in specific delivery order project assignments. � B. Department of the Air Force (DAF) Venture Gaming Program: The DAF Venture Gaming Program operates electronic gaming and slot machine activities at authorized overseas military installations. The program serves as an important nonappropriated revenue generator utilized directly to support and enhance Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs across all Air Force installations. Authorized by DoDI 1015.10 and centrally managed by AFSVC in San Antonio, TX, slot machine operations present unique risks due to regulatory complexities, high cash volumes, and potential for manipulation. Scope includes electronic gaming data systems, meter reconciliations, cash drop and count controls, payout authorizations, jackpot disbursements, internal control safeguards against manipulation or theft, and compliance with federal tax reporting requirements (including IRS Form W-2G processing). � C. Air Force Cadet Dining Fund: The Cadet Dining Fund is a Supplemental Mission Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) operated by the 10th Force Support Squadron (10th FSS) located at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), Colorado. Supplemental Mission NAFIs receive nonappropriated funds generated from installation mission programs (training, food service, education, security). While congressionally appropriated funds (APF) cover civilian management, custodial services, and facility upkeep, nonappropriated funds are utilized strictly for food purchases and the operational maintenance of cadet meal operations. The fund provides daily dining support for over 4,400 cadets. The Contractor shall perform comprehensive financial statement and operational compliance audits examining food supply procurement, inventory receiving and storage controls, cost-per-meal accounting, meal card verifications, and financial statement accuracy in accordance with USAFAI 34-104 and applicable NAF regulations. � D. Commander�s Special Interest Audits: To address immediate, unplanned operational needs, the Government requires the capacity to execute ad hoc, targeted investigations known as Commander�s Special Interest Audits. These audits may be requested at any given time by Installation Commanders, the AFSVC Commander, or higher headquarters to address immediate operational concerns, suspected material control failures, or strategic risk areas. These ad hoc engagements may encompass any Air Force Installation, NAF Activity, or fund within the scope of this contract, and will be ordered and executed as individual, consolidated performance audit task orders in accordance with the established deliverables and pricing schedules. title: Alternative Protein Technologies for Military Field Feeding
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command - Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC) to identify potential sources to provide innovative product development research and/or consumer research and/or demonstration food samples in the area of alternative proteins. Responses are limited to Massachusetts based offerors as determined by CAGE code. The Government requests responders submit a Broad Agency Announcement BAA preproposal as outlined in DEVCOM-SC BAA W911QY-25-R-0023 located at: https://sam.gov/opp/a5ec94e2baee40df9951f864a8665e71/view Please refer to Section VI - Scientific and Technical Areas of Interest, A. Combat Ration Research and Development. Submit the BAA preproposal to: michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil by 23 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. OBJECTIVE: DEVCOM-SC seeks product development, consumer research, and food sample demonstrations of current and emerging novel alternative protein technologies that could be integrated into military rations. BACKGROUND: The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Combat Feeding Division (CFD), is seeking information from industry and academia on capabilities related to alternative proteins. The U.S. Army is exploring how the emerging alternative-protein sector can help meet several objectives, including enhancing food supply chain resilience, enabling biomanufacturing of foodstuffs in combat-forward environments, and providing tailored, high-quality nutrition to the Warfighter. DEVCOM-SC CFD has unique expertise in the development and assessment of shelf-stable ration components, as well as food safety and palatability for the Joint Warfighter. We are looking to partner with the commercial and academic sectors to advance technology development in this area. AREAS OF INTEREST: DEVCOM-SC is seeking information from offerors that can provide capabilities in one or more of the following areas. Work proposed should be to advance technology between TRL 4 and 6. Please note, for the purposes of this Sources Sought, we are specifically excluding solutions related to cell-cultured, lab-grown meat or insect protein. Innovative technologies for alternative protein development to reduce Soldier load: Seeking advanced technologies and processes involved in fermentation, precision fermentation, or other novel biomanufacturing methods, that enhance the production of alternative proteins where additional funding in specific components of the research would significantly accelerate advancements in technology between TRL 4 and 6, enabling faster transition to operational use. These technologies should focus on creating lightweight and nutrient-dense ration solutions to reduce logistical burdens and physical load on warfighters while maintaining or enhancing nutritional value and operational performance. Innovative Product Development: The development of innovative meat-alternative products specifically designed for inclusion in military rations, meeting stringent requirements for nutrition, shelf stability, and palatability. Consumer Research and Acceptability: The ability to conduct comprehensive consumer research (e.g., focus groups, sensory panels, field testing) to enhance the acceptability and consumption of alternative proteins within a military population. Food Sample Demonstration: An optional addition to the effort would be to provide 100 food samples of a potential product that has Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) status with an FDA no-questions letter to demonstrate the maturation of an alternative protein manufacturing technology. These samples would be provided to the Government for sensory acceptability and other performance characteristics and will be consumed by our test panel of experts. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested parties (companies or academic institutions) are requested to submit a proposal that details their capabilities in one or more of the areas listed in Section 3.0. Submissions should include: A detailed description of your technical approach. Relevant past performance or corporate experience. A rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimate for the proposed work or samples. This information will be used for market research and planning purposes. Responses to this Sources Sought are not binding proposals, but they will help shape future solicitation requirements. Offerors are welcome to send samples at their own cost for evaluation. DEVCOM SC will not return any items, nor is DEVCOM SC obligated to share any data from evaluation. Sending samples is not required for consideration for funding. Samples must be GRAS with an FDA no-questions letter. Please coordinate by e-mail (richard.j.green.civ@army.mil) before sending samples. Address information will be provided at that time. SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This Sources Sought Announcement is issued solely for information and planning purposes and to identify interested sources. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. No contract will be awarded from this announcement. This Sources Sought does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. It is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. Further, unsolicited proposals will not be accepted. Funding is not available at this time. The United States Army has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this Sources Sought Announcement should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. Response to this Sources Sought Announcement is voluntary and no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this and any follow-on information requests. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Sources Sought Announcement does not preclude participation in any future RFP if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential responders to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this subject. RESPONSES: Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending BAA preproposals regarding this requirement to DEVCOM-SC via e-mail ONLY to michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil by 23 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice. All costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the expense of the interested party. Submissions should include: Whether you are proposing product development and/or consumer research and/or sample demonstration. A detailed description of your technical approach. Relevant past performance or corporate experience. A rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimate for the proposed work or samples. Please provide business size (indicate your socioeconomic status), applicable NAICS code, and CAGE code. QUESTIONS: Any questions for clarification may be emailed to michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil no later than 18 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. An unattributed list of questions and answers will be published at the same web location of this Sources Sought Announcement.

title: Delivery and installation of a ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics
description: DTU Nanolab wishes to acquire a high ion density source reactive ion etcher for oxides and nitrides of silicon to become its new primary instrument for 150 mm wafer processing. Delivery is expected no later than Q3 2027. The Instrument will be installed in the DTU Nanolab cleanroom - a university facility providing a comprehensive suite of micro- and nanofabrication tools. It serves a diverse community of over 200 active users, ranging from novice students to experienced researchers, as well a high percentage of commercial clients. As an open access tool, the Instrument must support the full spectrum of etching of silicon-based dielectrics, from sub 100 nm nanostructures defined by electron beam lithography to depths of several tens of microns. Meeting these demands requires exceptional process controllability and tunability: the system must perform ultra precise, low-rate etches (< 100 nm/min) with smooth and straight sidewalls and minimal undercut for shallow features, alongside high etch rate deep etches (approaching 500 nm/min). It must also accommodate all silicon dielectrics of the form SixNy, SixOx and SixOyNz, and be compatible with mask materials including Si, Cr, e-beam resists and UV/DUV photoresists with high mask selectivity for all these masking materials. The user interface must be intuitive and user friendly. The Instrument should be engineered to the highest industrial standards to minimize maintenance, and any required servicing must be straightforward and efficient. The instrument must be configured for 150 mm wafer processing and a complete kit enabling the processing of 200 mm wafers must be included in the tender as an option. Furthermore, DTU will have the option to purchase one more ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics identical to the initial instrument.

title: Udbud af hovedentreprisekontrakt med fast entreprisesum uden mulighed for regulering ved mængdeafvigelser vedrørende forstærkning af Ballum Dige
description: Digelaget i Brede Ådalen ("Digelaget") er en lokal forening, der står for vedligeholdelse og sikring af diger langs Brede Å for at forhindre oversvømmelser af de tilstødende landbrugsarealer og dalstrøg. Digelagets arbejde består derfor oftest i at vedligeholde digekroner og skråninger for at sikre stabilitet mod vandtryk. Digelaget ønsker nu på strækningen fra Rømø Dæmningen og sydpå til Vesterende, der udgør i alt ca. 7.500 meter, at få det eksisterende Ballum Dige forstærket med klæg og sand. Arbejdet vil også omfatte udgravning og tildannelse af søområde ifm indvinding af de til Ballum Dige benyttede sand- og klæg-forekomster. På denne baggrund ønsker Digelaget at indgå én bygge- og anlægskontrakt ("Kontrakten") med én fast entreprisesum uden mulighed for regulering ved mængdeafvigelser. Entreprenøren bærer mængderisikoen. Kontrakten vil i hovedtræk omfatte følgende arbejder (de anslåede mængder for hver af de nedenstående arbejder fremgår af tilbudslisten, der indgår som en del af det samlede udbudsmateriale): 1. Fræsning af vækstlaget på dige (på eksisterende diges forskråning, forland og digekrone) 2. Afgravning af vækstlag og midlertidig deponering heraf på eksisterende diges forskråning, forland, digekrone og på bagskråning 3. Opgravning fra eksisterende dige, flytning og indbygning af råjord i diget 4. Opgravning fra eksisterende dige og bortskaffelse af råjord i diget 5. Opgravning fra søerne, flytning og indbygning af klæg 6. Genudlægning af vækstlag samt græssåning på den nye digeprofil. Hertil suppleres med tilkørsel af vækstlagsjord fra søerne 7. De til entreprisen nødvendige mængder råjord og klæg indvindes af entreprenøren i forbindelse med udgravning af nye søer tæt ved delprojektet. Materialerne transporteres til diget og indbygges af entreprenøren. Søerne holdes tørre af entreprenøren i forbindelse med gravearbejderne 8. Færdiggørelse af søernes brinker og reetablering af berørte arealer omkring søerne 9. Gødskning og græssåning af alle berørte arealer Alle de arealer, hvor der skal udføres arbejder, er beliggende ved Ballum i Tønder Kommune. Det klæg, der skal anvendes til brug for forstrækningen, leveres som en bygherreleverance (estimerede værdi udgør ca. 15-16 mio. kr.). Selve transporten af klæget vil være omfattet af de arbejder, der er tilknyttet til Kontrakten. Foruden dette omfattes af Kontrakten et mindre supplerende indkøb og levering samt udlægning af egnet stabilt grus eller knust beton til vedligeholdelse af interimsveje og arbejdsveje fra opgravningssted frem til digets indbygningssteder. Digelaget kan ikke stille el til rådighed, men kan være behjælpelig. Arbejderne med selve digebyggeriet skal udføres fra marts/april 2027 til oktober 2028 i tidsrummet fra kl. 04.00–18.00, dog under forudsætning af at dette ikke strider imod øvrig regulering, herunder tilladelsen fra Kystdirektoratet. Dertil kommer, at det er forventningen, at arbejderne på opgravningsstederne kan påbegyndes cirka en måned tidligere, dvs. i februar 2027. Af hensyn til digesikkerheden er entreprenøren forpligtet til at holde pause i udførelsen fra og med oktober 2027 til februar 2028, hvorefter arbejderne kan genoptages. På tidspunktet for udbuddets offentliggørelse har Digelaget ikke modtaget endelig tilladelse fra Kystdirektoratet til kystbeskyttelse, ligesom Digelaget heller ikke på dette tidspunkt har modtaget udlednings- samt landzonetilladelse fra Tønder Kommune. På denne baggrund tager Digelaget derfor udtrykkeligt forbehold for at annullere udbuddet, hvis endelige tilladelser ikke opnås. Digelaget tager ligeledes udtrykkeligt forbehold for at afvente indgåelse af Kontrakten med den vindende tilbudsgiver, indtil de endelige tilladelser er opnået. Yderligere tager Digelaget udtrykkeligt forbehold for at annullere udbuddet, hvis Digelaget ikke modtager den nødvendige finansiering fra Tønder Kommune til projektets gennemførelse, ligesom Digelaget i dette tilfælde også tager udtrykkeligt forbehold for at afvente indgåelse af Kontrakten med den vindende tilbudsgiver. Digelaget har ikke opdelt den udbudte bygge- og anlægskontrakt i delkontrakter, idet Digelaget vurderer, at en sådan opdeling vil medføre en række uhensigtsmæssige tekniske, juridiske og praktiske grænseflader med deraf følgende risiko for forøgede transaktionsomkostninger og risikoeksponering for Digelaget. Særligt dokumenterne arbejdsbeskrivelse for arbejdsplads, arbejdsbeskrivelse for færdselsregulerende foranstaltninger, Asfalt - AAB-SAB-P, AAB-SAB-P SOS og AAB-SAB Jordarbejder indeholder en udførlig beskrivelse af de opgaver, som er omfattet af Kontrakten. Enhver henvisning til standarder skal forstås som en henvisning til den nævnte standard eller tilsvarende. Opfylder tilbudsgiver ikke den nævnte standard, men tilsvarende, skal tilbudsgiver i tilbuddet dokumentere, at den tilbudte løsning på de relevante parametre er tilsvarende. Udbuddet gennemføres elektronisk ved brug af udbudsportalen www.udbuddet.dk. Tilbudsgiver skal derfor oprettes som licenshaver hos www.udbuddet.dk. Oprettelse kan ske uden omkostning. Spørgsmål vedrørende www.udbuddet.dk skal stilles direkte via support-funktionen (tlf. 70227007). Der ydes ikke vederlag for tilbudsgivernes deltagelse i udbudsprocessen. Tilbudsgiverne opfordres til at foretage en besigtigelse af den strækning, hvor der skal ske forstærkning. Dette særligt af hensyn til, at Kontrakten udbydes med én fast entreprisesum uden mulighed for regulering ved mængdeafvigelser. Det betyder, at entreprenørens vederlag ikke reguleres, uanset om de anførte mængder i tilbudslisten, der danner grundlag for beregning af den faste entreprisesum, måtte vise sig anderledes under udførelsen. Derfor kan Bygherre også stille de 3D-målinger, der danner grundlag for mængderne i tilbudslisten, til rådighed som en del af udbudsmaterialet.

buyer: Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation
title: Denmark – Industrial robots – Udbud af kontrakt om udvikling, levering, installation og servicering af nyt desarmeringsanlæg til Forsvaret
description: Hermed udbyder FMI (i det følgende ”Ordregiver”) på vegne af Forsvaret, herunder Ammunitionsrydningskompagniet (ARKMP) ved Hærens Ingeniørregiment (IGR) en kontrakt om gennemførelse af et forprojekt om udvikling og efterfølgende levering, installation og servicering af et nyt desarmeringsanlæg til Forsvaret. Kontrakten indbefatter endvidere nedtagning af det eksisterende anlæg. Desarmeringsanlægget, der findes på Operationsområde Aflandshage på Sydamager, bruges til undersøgelse, adskillelse og desarmering af potentielt farlige fundne genstande. Anlægget findes i et til formålet opført og indrettet bygningskompleks. Bygningskomplekset indeholder gennemgående spor for køretøj, rum med 4 sprængningssikre skakte til opbevaring af genstandene, rum til placering af røntgensystem, manipulatorrum med robotsystem og et sikret operatørrum, hvor systemerne betjenes fra. Det eksisterende anlæg består af en ABB-industrirobot model IRB2000 M91 med tilhørende værktøjer, manipulatorbord, videodokumentationssystem med kameraer samt røntgensystem, som er anskaffet i 1992, da desarmeringsanlægget blev opført på Farum kaserne. Systemet i desarmeringsanlægget er af ældre dato og er derfor udfordret bl.a. ved mangel på reservedele. Der er derfor taget initiativ til at igangsætte en proces for anskaffelse af et nyt anlæg, der kan udføre alle de nødvendige funktioner. Anskaffelsen vedrører et forprojekt om udvikling og efterfølgende levering, installation og servicering af robotten inklusiv værktøjer, manipulatoren og videodokumentationssystemet med kameraer. Der indkøbes en ny røntgenkilde i en separat anskaffelsesproces. Leverandøren af desarmeringsanlægget er ikke teknisk ansvarlig for røntgenkilden, men skal dog designe, fremstille og installere sin løsning, så røntgensystemet og Leverandørens desarmeringsanlæg kan operere sammen. Med værktøjer forstås forskellige redskaber, der kan påsættes robotten, og som kan klippe, save, skære, skrue, bore og gribe i emnerne på manipulatoren. Derudover skal den valgte leverandør også nedtage den nuværende ABB-robot inklusiv værktøjer, manipulatorbord, videodokumentationssystem med kameraer samt røntgenkilden som nævnt ovenfor. Ordregiver sørger selv for bortskaffelsen af det nedtagne robotanlæg mv. fra lokationen på Aflandshage. Udbuddet gennemføres som et udbud med forhandling, med offentliggørelse af en udbudsbekendtgørelse i medfør af udbudslovens § 61, stk. 1, nr. 1, litra a, c og d. Udbuddet gennemføres som et udbud med forhandling fordi, at Ordregivers behov ikke kan imødekommes uden tilpasning af tilgængelige løsninger i markedet, bl.a. henset til at der er behov for teknisk afklaring af en væsentlig snitflade til det samtidigt indkøbte røntgensystem, og idet løsningen skal tilpasses Ordregivers behov for uddannelse af sit personale. Anskaffelsen foretages desuden i et meget dynamisk marked, hvorfor det er vanskeligt at fastsætte tekniske specifikationer, der rammer markedets aktuelle udviklingsstadie, og som samtidig er fleksible nok til at muliggøre fremtidige systemmæssige tilpasninger og opdateringer, jf. i det hele litra a. Herudover kompliceres opgaven ved, at installationen, der bl.a. indbefatter en omfattende kabelføring, og den efterfølgende servicering skal foretages i et sprængningssikret bunkermiljø med ofte meget lave temperaturer. Anskaffelsens art og samlede kompleksitet, nødvendiggør således en proces, der giver mulighed for at forhandle med de egnede virksomheder om den bedste løsning, jf. litra c. Endelig lader det sig ikke gøre med en tilstrækkelig præcision at fastlægge de tekniske specifikationer med henvisning til en standard, europæisk teknisk vurdering, fælles teknisk specifikation eller teknisk reference, jf. litra d, da anskaffelsens kompleksitet i høj grad betinges af de konkrete forhold, som opgaven skal udføres under.

title: Spain – Hotel accommodation services – concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana (C-2026/032)
description: El objeto del presente contrato es la concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana, de titularidad municipal, situado en el municipio de Alcalá de Guadaíra, que comprende la gestión integral del establecimiento, así como la ejecución de las actuaciones necesarias de rehabilitación, reforma, posible ampliación y adecuación del inmueble para su correcto funcionamiento y mejora de categoría, todo ello conforme a lo establecido en el correspondiente pliego de prescripciones técnicas. La presente contratación tiene como finalidad la transformación integral del establecimiento hotelero, con el objetivo de su adecuación a los estándares actuales del sector y su posicionamiento como hotel de cuatro estrellas, mediante la ejecución de las actuaciones constructivas necesarias y la implantación de un modelo de gestión profesionalizado, eficiente y orientado a la calidad. No se pretende con esta licitación una mera explotación del establecimiento en su estado actual, sino la definición y desarrollo de un proyecto global y coherente que integre la intervención sobre el inmueble con un modelo de gestión hotelera alineado con el valor patrimonial, paisajístico y turístico del entorno en el que se inserta, contribuyendo a reforzar la identidad y singularidad del destino. En este sentido, la concesión deberá orientarse a la creación de una oferta hotelera de calidad, capaz de atraer tanto a visitantes como a usuarios locales, generando actividad económica, empleo y sinergias con otros sectores vinculados al turismo, la cultura y la hostelería, y actuando como elemento dinamizador del municipio y su entorno. Asimismo, el contrato comprende tanto la ejecución de las obras definidas como obligatorias, como, en su caso, la incorporación de mejoras propuestas por los licitadores, así como la gestión integral del establecimiento, incluyendo todos los servicios necesarios para su correcto funcionamiento. El detalle y alcance de todas estas prestaciones se desarrollan en el pliego de prescripciones técnicas que rige la presente contratación.

Die Möblierung soll eine flexible Nutzung der Räume ermöglichen, zur Produktivität beitragen und ein ansprechendes, zeitgemäßes Arbeitsumfeld schaffen, das sowohl individuellen Rückzug als auch interaktive Zusammenarbeit unterstützt. description: The Mitigation Action Facility (MAF), formerly known as the NAMA Facility, is a multi-donor initiative established to support developing countries and emerging economies in implementing ambitious climate change mitigation measures and achieving their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. Its donors include Germany, the United Kingdom, Denmark, the European Commission and the Children"s Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF), which have provided more than EUR 835 million since its inception. The MAF focuses on the energy, transport and industry sectors, supporting projects with high potential for transformational change towards low-carbon development. Through annual competitive calls for proposals, it provides grants of EUR 5-25 million for technical and financial cooperation, with a particular emphasis on mobilising public and private investment in low-carbon technologies and infrastructure. On behalf of the MAF Board, the German government has commissioned GIZ to implement the Facility. GIZ provides the Technical Support Unit (TSU), which acts as the MAF secretariat, and serves as Grant Agent (Trustee). Individual projects are implemented by qualified Implementation Organisations (IOs), which provide the necessary technical and financial support.

title: Germany – Accounting software package – Digitaler Rechnungseingangsworkflow in SAP S/4 HANA
description: Das Universitätsklinikum Würzburg zählt zu den wichtigsten medizinischen Zentren in Deutschland und nimmt als einziges Krankenhaus der Supramaximalversorgung in Unterfranken eine herausragende Stellung in der medizinischen Versorgung ein. Jährlich profitieren rund 350.000 Patientinnen und Patienten von der intensiven interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit in 19 Kliniken und mehr als 60 interdisziplinären Zentren. Das UKW steht für internationale Spitzenleistungen in Krankenversorgung, Forschung und Lehre sowie für innovative und sichere Diagnostik, Therapie und Prävention. Eine besondere Stärke der Universitätsmedizin Würzburg ist die enge und praxisorientierte Kombination von Klinik und Forschung zur sicheren Anwendung neuer Methoden. Gemeinsam mit der Medizinischen Fakultät ist das UKW eine der großen Ausbildungsstätten für Medizinerinnen und Mediziner in Deutschland. Die Verteilung von mehr als 70 unterschiedlichen Bereichen auf verschiedene Standorte innerhalb Würzburgs sowie die Beteiligung von bis zu 1.500 Personen am Rechnungsfreigabeprozess stellen das Klinikum vor besondere organisatorische Herausforderungen. Das UKW verarbeitet pro Jahr rund 150.000 Belege von etwa 9.500 unterschiedlichen Kreditoren. Das Ziel der Ausschreibung ist es eine zukunftsorientierte Lösung zur digitalen, medienbruchfreien Rechnungsverarbeitung und Workflowsteuerung in einer integrierten SAP-nahen Lösung zu erhalten, welche die bisherige Lösung Tangro IM (Invoice Management) und Tangro BWF (Business Workflow) bis spätestens 30.09.2027 vollumfänglich ablöst. Das System muss dabei sowohl einfache lineare Freigabeprozesse als auch komplexe, regelbasierte und mehrstufige Genehmigungsverfahren abbilden können. Wichtig ist hierbei die Anpassungsfähigkeit an gesetzliche Rahmenbedingungen, beispielsweise im Zuge der E-Rechnungspflicht, sowie die flexible Steuerung der Workflows bei organisatorischen Prozessänderungen. Das Universitätsklinikum Würzburg (UKW) setzt SAP S/4HANA als zentrales ERP-System und führende Systemplattform für die kaufmännischen Prozesse, insbesondere die Finanzbuchhaltung, ein. Im Rahmen der Rechnungsverarbeitung soll SAP S/4HANA grundsätzlich als führendes System dienen, in dem rechnungsbezogene Prozesse und Informationen - soweit fachlich und technisch möglich - zentral verarbeitet und revisionssicher nachvollziehbar abgebildet werden. Angeschlossene Systeme und Anwendungen sollen sich entsprechend in die bestehende SAP-Systemlandschaft integrieren und erforderliche Informationen an SAP S/4HANA übergeben bzw. daraus beziehen. Die Lösung ist in einem hybriden Betriebsmodell bereitzustellen. Funktionen zur Erfassung, Digitalisierung und Interpretation von Rechnungsbelegen können in der Cloud des Auftragnehmers erbracht werden. Weitere Komponenten werden auf der vom UKW bereitgestellten Serverinfrastruktur betrieben. Die weitere Verarbeitung einschließlich Prüfung, Kontierung, Genehmigungsworkflow und Buchung muss vollständig und integriert innerhalb des SAP-S/4HANA-Systems erfolgen. Die Lösung muss einen durchgängigen, medienbruchfreien Prozess gewährleisten und eine revisionssichere Nachvollziehbarkeit der rechnungsbezogenen Vorgänge ermöglichen. Die erforderlichen Schnittstellen und der Datenaustausch zwischen den Cloud-Komponenten, der lokalen Infrastruktur und SAP S/4HANA sind vom Auftragnehmer bereitzustellen und zu dokumentieren.

buyer: Zweckverband Industriepark Schwarze Pumpe (ZV ISP) vertreten durch die ASG Spremberg GmbH als Treuhänder
title: Germany – Engineering services – Industriepark Schwarze Pumpe; Modernisierung der Hydrolyse auf der Abwasserbehandlungsanlage I (ABA I); Planungsleistungen LP 1-9
description: Die anaerobe/aerobe biologische Kläranlage (ABA I) im Industriepark Schwarze Pumpe ist Eigentum des Zweckverbandes Industriepark Schwarze Pumpe und wird von der ASG Spremberg GmbH betrieben. Die ABA I verarbeitet Abwässer von den Erschließungsflächen gemäß Standortentwässerungskonzept, u.a. auch der Papiermaschine PM1 der Papierfabrik Spremberg. Zudem ist die ABA I so konzipiert, dass Abwässer mit hoch belasteten CSB-Konzentrationen abgebaut werden können. Zur Vorbehandlung des Abwassers vor den Anaerobreaktoren wird eine sogenannte Hydrolysestufe betrieben. In dieser Behandlungsstufe dient ein Behälter für die benötigte Vorversäuerung und Pufferung des zufließenden Abwassers. In den zurückliegenden Betriebsjahren gab es grundlegende Änderungen in der Charakteristik des Zuflusses aus der Papierfabrik. Mit Errichtung der Abwasserbehandlungsanlage 2 am Standort des Industrieparks Schwarze Pumpe wurde unter anderen das Produktspektrum der Einleiter angepasst. Weiterhin bezieht die Papiermaschine 1 ihr Brauchwassers von der Lausitz Energie Bergbau AG (LEAG). In den zurückliegenden Jahren ist die Qualität dieses Brauchwassers kontinuierlich schlechter geworden bezüglich des Sulfatgehaltes. Durch einen Anstieg des Sulfatgehaltes kommt es zu einer erhöhten Schwefelwasserstoffkonzentration, wodurch die Korrosionsbildung innerhalb der Behandlungsstufe weiter fortschreitet. Der Gehalt an Sulfat im Zulauf zur ABA I wird in den nächsten Jahren weiter zunehmen. Verfahrenstechnisch bedingt wird die Hydrolysestufe mit feststoffhaltigem Abwasser beschickt. Im Betrieb kommt es trotz des Eintrages von Turbulenzen mittels eines Rührwerkes vermehrt zu Problemen durch größere Ablagerungen sedimentierter Feststoffe in der Hydrolyse. Durch die Ablagerungen entstehen hierdurch große Totvolumen, die die Funktionsweise negativ beeinflussen. Weiterhin erfolgte in den letzten Jahren eine Erhöhung der Abwassermenge, wodurch eine ausreichende Verweilzeit des Abwassers innerhalb der Hydrolysestufe nicht dauerhaft sichergestellt werden kann. Zur Gewährleistung eines stabilen Weiterbetriebes der ABA I ist eine Modernisierung der Hydrolysestufe und eine damit verbundene Anpassung an den aktuellen Stand der Technik zwingend erforderlich. Aufgrund der zunehmenden Aggressivität des behandelten Abwassers ist eine Anpassung des Behältermaterials auf Edelstahl geplant. In Anbetracht der oben erwähnten Änderungen hinsichtlich der Charakteristik der zufließenden Abwasserströme wird im Rahmen der Modernisierung eine bedarfsgerechte Erweiterung der Hydrolysestufe angestrebt. Durch die geplante Erhöhung des Behandlungsvolumens der Hydrolysestufe werden vermehrt verfahrenstechnische Redundanzen für einen stabileren Betrieb der ABA I geschaffen.

A key part of this effort is the GovTech Innovation Programme, which accelerates startups and the creation of inclusive technological products that enhance government services and responsiveness to citizens' needs and 3) provides support for the development of forward-looking digital strategies and legal frameworks in emerging areas such as trust services, artificial intelligence, and data-driven decision-making, in line with EU digitalization standards. EU-German Action Digital Transformation in the Southern Neighbourhood The programme "Digital Transformation in the Southern Neighbourhood" was initiated in February 2026 and is co-funded by the European Commission Directorate General MENA (DG MENA), the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), and the German Federal Foreign Office (FFO). The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) has been commissioned to implement the three project components and implements the activities from Germany, Spain and additional regional hubs. In partnership with governments in the region, the programme strives to accelerate the Southern Neighbourhood"s digital transformation through targeted support across three critical areas: cybersecurity, digital regulation, and digital skills. The second specific objective on improved Prevention, preparedness and response of relevant stakeholders in the South-ern Neighbourhood with regards to cyber threats is pertinent for this tender. It comprises the following pillars: 1. Strengthened national legal frameworks and cybersecurity governance in line with international standards and frameworks for responsible state behaviour in cyberspace. Support will include technical assistance for the drafting, revision and implementation of national cybersecurity strategies, laws, and policies, in line with international frameworks and the EU"s Cybersecurity Strategy. 2. Improved operational capacities, such as prevention, preparedness and response, for cyber incident management and inter-agency cooperation. This includes hands-on training, development of operational procedures, provision of technical tools, and facilitation of simulation exercises to improve threat response and incident management. 3. Established community of stakeholders for sharing best practices and incident information at regional, trans-regional and international level. In this framework joint activities such as regional table-top exercises, joint threat analysis workshops, and mentorship programmes for mid-career professionals will be explored.

title: Germany – Urban environmental development planning – 10012255-Short Term Expert Support on Sustainable and Inclusive Mobility in Colombia
description: ProMOVIS II, implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), supports Colombian cities in strengthening their capacities to deliver public transport systems that better serve their populations. Colombia has committed to ambitious climate targets under its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), requiring a 51% reduction in projected emissions by 2030. The transport sector accounts for approximately 45% of energy related GHG emissions nationwide, making the decarbonization of urban transport one of the country's most impactful mitigation opportunities. Despite ongoing efforts, the integration of public transport systems at local and regional levels remains insufficient, affected by the lasting effects of the pandemic, financing gaps, low digitalization, and early stage regional integration, particularly critical in metropolitan regions with high intermunicipal commuting, such as Valle del Cauca. Within this context, ProMOVIS II concentrates technical cooperation efforts on strengthening public transportation, incorporating a regional integration perspective and initially focusing its actions on Valle del Cauca. The objective is that public transport in selected Colombian cities is more integrated, inclusive and environmentally friendly, pursued through three outcomes: (1) number of people benefiting from newly created or improved public transport; (2) funds secured by selected cities to finance environmentally friendly, integrated public transport projects; and (3) number of bus operators and transport authorities that assess that professionals trained in green jobs training formats contribute positively to integrated, inclusive and environmentally friendly public transport. Through technical assistance, financing-related support, and knowledge exchange, ProMOVIS II addresses the institutional, organizational and operational challenges that limit the effective integration and sustainability of public transport systems, working closely with national and local governments, transport authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen local capacities and develop solutions that are replicable, scalable and sustainable over time.

buyer: Kreis Herford im Auftrag der Widukindstadt Enger
title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Widukindstadt Enger, Sanierung und Erweiterung der Turnhalle der Grundschule Belke-Steinbeck/Besenkamp - Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume
description: Die Widukindstadt Enger plant die umfassende energetische Sanierung und Modernisierung der 1-fach Turnhalle auf dem Grundstück der Grundschule Belke-Steinbeck/Besenkamp in der Humboldtstraße 20 in Enger. Im Rahmen der Maßnahme sollen sowohl der Hallenbereich als auch die Umkleidebereiche bis auf den Rohbau zurückgebaut werden, um eine vollständige bauliche und technische Erneuerung zu ermöglichen. Im Fokus der Modernisierung stehen die energetische Aufwertung der Fensterfront im Hallenteil, der Einbau eines neuen Hallenbodens und die Installation einer modernen Lüftungsanlage mit Wärmerückgewinnung. Für die Beheizung der Halle ist eine Deckenstrahlungsheizung vorgesehen. Die Beleuchtung, Lüftung und das Heizsystem sollen künftig durch den Einsatz erneuerbarer Energien - darunter eine Wärmepumpe sowie eine Photovoltaikanlage - betrieben werden. Mit Abschluss der Sanierungsmaßnahmen wird angestrebt, erstmals mindestens die Effizienzgebäude-Stufe 70 zu erreichen und somit einen hohen energetischen Standard sicherzustellen. Ein zentrales Ziel des Projektes ist zudem die Herstellung einer vollständigen Barrierefreiheit. Hierzu ist vorgesehen, die Turnhalle um eine behindertengerechte Umkleide mit WC- und Duschbereich zu erweitern, um allen Nutzergruppen einen gleichberechtigten und selbstständigen Zugang zu ermöglichen. Das Gebäude soll gemäß der Zertifizierungsprogrammes "Qualitätssiegel Nachhaltiges Bauen (QNG)" mit dem Status "PLUS" zertifiziert werden.

Målet är att skapa en välfungerande försörjningslösning med rätt servicenivå, hög tillgänglighet och god samverkan mellan leverantören och Region Dalarna, så att verksamheternas behov tillgodoses på ett ändamålsenligt och kvalitetssäkrat sätt. Det totala behovet av efterfrågade tjänster under aktuell avtalsperiod beräknas uppgå till 8 miljoner kronor, 2 miljoner kronor per år.

description: ********************************AMENDMENT 0001************************************* Amendment 0001 to SIR 6973GH-26-R-00199 is issued to re-open the SIR, extend the close date of the SIR, answer un-posted questions from industry that were received within the allowed question and answer SIR period, update the Schedule B. If you have previously provided a proposal to SIR 6973GH-26-R-00199, the contracting officer will be reach out with instructions. FOURTH: Clause AC1604 CONTRACT PERIOD is updated to make the new period of performance (POP) as follows: The effective period of this contract is 1 year from 01/19/2027, plus four, 1-year options if exercised. FIFTH: Schedule B dated 07/08/2026 is removed and replace by Schedule B Rev. 1 dated 11/06/2026. The Schedule B is updated to correct description of the Bell 412 Maintenance Initial Training. The POP is also updated to reflect the new POP. SIXTH: M.8 Evaluation Criteria Factor 5 is removed and replaced with the following language: FACTOR 4: THE OFFEROR MUST PROVIDE THE QUALIFICATION STATEMENTS AND RESUMES OF THE INSTRUCTORS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PWS & THE SOLICITATION. CRITERIA: Persons utilized as instructors must provide evidence of professional technician�s experience as outlined in Section G.5 of the PWS. a. A professional Maintenance Technician with five (5) years of industry experience. b. Minimum of three (3) years of experience with each aircraft being proposed under Section A; AND c. Minimum of three (3) years of instructor experience ACCEPTABLE: The Standard is met when the offeror meets provides qualification statements and resumes of the instructors to meet the requirements of section G.5 of the PWS and solicitation requirements. SEVENTH: Clause AC0250 was included in error and has been removed. EIGHTH: All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. ****************************************************************************** The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC), Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, has a requirement for Helicopter Field Maintenance Training IAW Air Transport Association (ATA) 104 Specifications for Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Airworthiness (Maintenance/Avionics) Inspectors on the following helicopters: Bell 206B Field Maintenance Training, Bell 429 Field Maintenance Training, Bell 407 Field Maintenance Training and Bell 412 Maintenance Initial Training. It is the intent of the Government to award multiple contract(s) using an Indefinite Delivery/Requirements type Contract priced by CLIN with student qualifier for a one (1) year base period and four (4) option years, if exercised. The Government intends to award multiple contracts. The intent is to award each aircraft type to the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) Offeror. Each aircraft requirement is identified by separate CLINs in Schedule B and competition will be on an aircraft by aircraft basis. Resulting contract will be awarded to the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) Offeror per aircraft. The awarded contract(s) may contain many, few, or one aircraft depending on the competition results. NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE. ALL QUESTIONS MUST BE IN WRITING AND EMAILED TO THE CONTRACTING SPECIALIST. CONTACT INFORMATION BELOW. All interested sources should first attempt to download the attached SIR and supporting document(s). If downloading is not possible, all request for copies of the SIR documents(s) must be made in writing to the attention of Gilbert Park, Contracting Specialist (AAQ-740), via e-mail at gilbert.n.park@faa.gov. Any and all questions pertaining to this SIR should be submitted in writing to the contract specialist at, gilbert.n.park@faa.gov by 3:00 p.m. CST on August 10, 2026 to allow for adequate response time. No questions will be allowed after that date and time. Technical and cost proposals must be received by the FAA no later than 5:00 P.M. CST, August 26, 2026. Proposals must be submitted electronically to gilbert.n.park@faa.gov, and addressed with the SIR Number 6973GH-26- R-00199. All submittals will need to allow sufficient time to process through security procedures in place at the Aeronautical Center. In accordance with SIR Section L provision 3.2.2.3-14 entitled, "Late Submissions, Modifications, and Withdrawals of Submittals," any proposals received after the due time and date of 5:00 p.m. CST, August 26, 2026, will not be considered. In addition, if all requested information is not furnished in the offeror's proposal, the offeror's proposal may be determined to be non-responsive and ineligible for consideration for contract award. The SIR/RFO is not to be construed as a contract or a commitment of any kind. The Government shall not be liable for payment of any costs attributed to the preparation and submission of requested proposal documentation. title: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Port Angeles Annual Fire Protection System Inspection
description: DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: The U.S. Coast Guard requires annual inspection, testing, and maintenance of the fire protection systems for multiple facilities located at USCG AIRSTA Port Angeles. The work consists of providing all labor, equipment, material, transportation, supervision, items and services necessary for properly performing inspection, testing, and maintenance of fire protection systems in multiple buildings, including an aircraft hangar, in accordance with NFPA 11, NFPA 25, NFPA 70, NFPA 72, and NFPA 80 at Air Station Port Angeles. The Government intends to issue a firm-fixed-price purchase order for this project. The full scope of work and specifications are included in the solicitation documents. PROJECT ADDRESS: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Port Angeles 1 Ediz Hook Road Port Angeles, WA 98362 United States Classification: This acquisition is set-aside 100% for SMALL BUSINESS. The associated NAICS code is 541990 - Classified as All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services cross referenced as Waterless fire suppression system testing and/or inspection, without sales, service, or installation. The contract type will be firm fixed price purchase order. Where Federal Acquisition Regulation clause language is inconsistent with FAR 13.004, Legal Effect of Quotations, that language is hereby tailored in accordance with FAR 12.302 to be consistent with a request for quotations. This tailoring includes but is not limited to the following: In accordance with FAR 13.004, a quotation is not an offer, and any clause provision to the contrary is hereby modified to be consistent with FAR 13.004. Where the word "offer/offeror" or a derivative of that word appears, it is changed to "quote/quoter" or a derivative of that word. Site Visit: There will be no site visits held for this solicitation. Questions: Any and all questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer at patrick.r.gittings@uscg.mil with solicitation RFQ number 70ZL3227Q20190001 in subject line. Questions regarding the statement of work (SOW) will be forwarded to the technical expert for an accurate response. All responses will be uploaded for an equal and fair solicitation to all interested vendors solely on SAM.gov. No more questions will be answered after 3:00 PM PDT on November 19th, 2026. Quote submission: Prohibition on Extraneous Material: Do not submit any unnecessary documents, promotional marketing materials, general company history brochures, or generic cover letters. Quotes must contain only the specific information requested below. Extraneous documents will not be evaluated. Quotes must be submitted electronically to patrick.r.gittings@uscg.mil by the date and time specified in this solicitation. Incomplete submissions may be considered unresponsive and submissions that fail to adhere to these instructions may be considered disqualified and ineligible for award. A complete submission shall consist of the following parts: SF 1449: Complete and sign the provided Standard Form (SF) 1449. COMPLETE BLOCKS 12, 17, 20, 23, 24, AND 30, with a breakdown of all costs listed in block 20 and with the total firm-fixed-price bid in block 24. Technical Proposal: The Technical Proposal shall not exceed two (2) pages in length. It must provide a clear, concise narrative demonstrating the quoter�s understanding of and ability to meet the requirements of the Statement of Work (SOW). The proposal must include: 1. Technical Approach: A step-by-step description of how the quoter will perform the work in accordance with the Scope of Work. 2. Project Schedule: A high-level timeline illustrating the project's major milestones. The schedule must start from the date of the Notice to Award (NTA) and demonstrate that all work, including performance verification and report submission, will be completed within the required Period of Performance. Milestones should be shown in terms of days from the NTA (e.g., "Inspection of System(s) Complete: Day 3," "System(s) Repaired: Day 6," "Final Acceptance Testing: Day 9"). Submit quotes to the following E-mail Address Patrick.R.Gittings@uscg.mil with solicitation RFQ number 70ZL3227Q20190001 in the subject line. Date of offers due on 11/23/2026 at 3pm (PST). All offers that are submitted late (by day and time zone) and quotes that do not include a complete submission will not be considered in award determination. Award: It is the government�s intent to award to the offeror who proposes a price that is fair and reasonable and provides the lowest priced, technically acceptable (LPTA) quote meeting the specifications of the requirement. If the lowest priced quote is not found to be technically acceptable, the contracting officer will evaluate the next lowest priced quote, and so on. Quotes determined to be incomplete, unreasonable, or unrealistic will not be considered for award. Under FAR 4.1103 prospective contractor shall be registered in System Award Management (SAM) prior to award. Failure for contractor to be registered in SAM shall result in Contracting Officer to proceed with next successful registered offeror. Website: www.sam.gov.

title: Portugal – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Framework contract for EUDA scientific studies support services
description: The purpose of this procurement procedure is to purchase capacity to support the Agency in the preparation of high-quality scientific services and overall to increase the Agency’s timeliness, anticipatory and responsive capacity. The Agency requires access to supporting specialised expertise in the design, conduct, and reporting of different types of scientific work. Outputs may include reports, digital dashboards, AI based tools, methodological and reporting guidelines, training materials, workshops, databases, collection of literature, etc. The present procurement procedure is aimed at supporting the Agency to rapidly mobilise external expertise in a flexible and efficient manner, ensuring responsiveness to evolving scientific priorities and emerging evidence needs. The activities resulting from this procedure are expected to support the EUDA in monitoring drug markets, use of substances and their consequences. They will also help identify the evidence needed to inform responses in terms of establishing trends, examining emerging threats and tracking developments over time and between settings. Ultimately, this is expected to strengthen the preparedness of the Agency, and of the EU as a whole, to respond to drug-related harms.
